newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvador rights chief complains of death threats.
newsitem.headline: Salvador rights chief complains of death threats.

text.p: El Salvador's top human rights official said on Tuesday she had received numerous death threats and urged the United Nations to stay in the country to avoid damage to the fragile peace process.

"The situation has grown worse -- not only for me but for my family -- and it is casting doubt over the will to continue the peace process once the United Nations withdraws," Human Rights Attorney General Victoria de Aviles told reporters.
The United Nations keeps a small office in San Salvador overseeing the 1992 peace accords that put an end to a 12-year civil war. It is due to close down that mission in December.

As part of the healing process, the former left-wing Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front guerrillas demanded the establishment of a government human rights office. Her position there, Aviles said, meant she had been branded as a communist in the right-wing press.
She has some 400 employees in 14 provinces of El Salvador and an annual budget of $3 million.
About 75,000 people were killed in El Salvador's civil war,which pitted right-wing forces and shadowy death squads against the marxist rebels.
